workflows.name: Log weekly Google Ads Transparency creatives to Google Sheets with Apify alerts via Slack or email
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Each week this workflow runs the Google Ads Transparency Scraper Actor on Apify for a list of advertiser names or domains, appends only new creatives to a Google Sheet, and sends a Slack or email alert when something new appears after the first baseline run.

How it works
Runs on a Monday weekly schedule (or manually for testing) and loads configuration such as advertiser queries, region/format filters, and notification settings.
Calls the Apify Google Ads Transparency Scraper Actor with the configured queries and limits, and retrieves the resulting dataset.
Filters the Apify dataset to keep only rows that represent ads and include a creativeId.
Reads existing rows from the target Google Sheets tab and compares creativeId values to detect creatives not already logged.
Appends any newly found creatives to Google Sheets with metadata like advertiser, dates shown, URLs, and timestamps.
If this is not the baseline run and new creatives were added, sends a digest alert to either Slack or email based on your notifyVia setting.

Setup
Install the verified community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify (n8n 1.57.0 or later). On n8n Cloud, the instance owner may need to allow verified community nodes. See https://docs.apify.com/integrations/n8n
Connect an Apify API credential (API token from Apify Console → Settings → Integrations / API). Do not paste tokens into the workflow.
Connect Google Sheets, plus Slack or SMTP, matching notifyVia in the configuration node.
In Configure weekly check, set queries (one advertiser name or domain per line), region, format, maxAdsPerAdvertiser, notifyVia (slack or email), and the Google Sheet ID.
Create a Google Sheet whose first row is: creativeId, advertiserName, advertiserId, format, firstShown, lastShown, daysShown, adUrl, query, region, imageUrl, previewUrl, scrapedAt, loggedAt. Use the sheet name in the configuration node (default Ad creatives).
Run the workflow once with the manual trigger to build the baseline, then enable the Monday schedule. Alerts for new creatives start on later runs.

Requirements
Required package: @apify/n8n-nodes-apify (tested with 0.9.0 on n8n 2.47.7)

Additional info
List price is $0.0015 per ad saved on the Apify Free plan; paid plans are slightly lower. The Actor also writes one advertiser summary per advertiser; confirm that event on the Store Pricing tab (listed at $0.01 in the Actor's event pricing). This template does not set previousRunDatasetId, so it does not incur change-alert charges; new creatives are detected by comparing the sheet. A default of 3 advertisers × 50 ads is up to about $0.23 in ad charges, plus any summary charges. maxTotalChargeUsd on the Apify node is a hard cap (0.50 in this template). Leave extractAdText off unless you have separately confirmed that option for your use case.

workflows.name: Create daily outreach leads and Gmail drafts from Google Maps with Apify and Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every weekday at 6 AM, scrapes Google Maps via Apify to find new businesses for rotating search-and-city pairs, logs them to Google Sheets, and creates Gmail drafts from your own template (never sent) using role-based inboxes discovered from each company’s website.

How it works
Runs on a schedule Monday to Friday at 6 AM (or can be started manually).
Finds an existing Google Sheet by name in Google Drive or creates it with a Leads tab and header row on the first run.
Reads existing leads from Google Sheets, rotates to today’s search and city, and uses Apify’s Google Maps Scraper to fetch up to 20 places.
Filters out closed listings, places without websites, and any company whose website domain already exists in the sheet, keeping up to the configured daily limit.
Uses Apify’s Website Contact Extractor to crawl each website and select a role-based inbox address (for example info@ or hello@) while ignoring personal-looking addresses.
For companies still missing an inbox, runs Apify’s Website Email Scraper and applies the same role-inbox selection rules to fill any remaining gaps.
Appends one row per new company to the Google Sheets Leads tab and creates a Gmail draft for each lead that has an inbox using the configured subject/body template.

Setup
Install the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify and add Apify credentials for the Apify nodes.
Add Google Sheets OAuth credentials (used for both Google Sheets and Google Drive/Sheets HTTP requests) so the workflow can find or create the spreadsheet and write to the Leads tab.
Add Gmail credentials and confirm you are comfortable with the workflow creating drafts only (it does not send emails).
Update the Settings values (sheet name, searches, cities, daily lead limit, sender name, and the email subject/body template placeholders) to match your outreach needs.

Requirements
An Apify account, the Google Sheets/Drive and Gmail credentials, and the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify. Cost in our tests was about $0.08 per daily run at Apify Store prices (10 new companies); the Maps search costs about $0.02 even on days with no new companies. Each Apify node has a maximum cost per run.

Customization
Edit the Settings node: one search per line, one city per line (one search × city pair per weekday), newPerDay, sender name, and the subject/body with {company}, {city}, {category} and {sender} placeholders. The role-inbox list (info, hello, events, sales, …) is in the inbox-picking Code node.

Additional info
How this differs from existing Google Maps outreach templates: most of them send the email for you (one email per lead, a CSV mailed to you, or an automated sequence). This one never sends: it only creates Gmail drafts you review. It writes only to role inboxes the company publishes on its own website, never to a person's address. It runs daily and incrementally (known domains are skipped, N new per day, rotating searches), needs no AI key, Airtable or CRM, and creates its own Sheet on the first run. Whether you may email a company depends on your country's rules; check before you send.

workflows.name: Find and score LinkedIn buyers at funded accounts with Apify, OpenAI and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Outbound that starts with timing. Each week this checks your target accounts on Crunchbase, keeps those at the funding stages that buy from you, runs a LinkedIn people search for your buyer title, and has OpenAI score each person and draft an email. Strong fits reach Slack.

How it works
A schedule trigger starts the run every Monday, and a Set node holds your accounts, stages, buyer title and ideal customer.
The first Actor looks each account up on Crunchbase by name or domain: funding rounds, lead investors, headcount, industries and recent news.
A Code node takes the newest real round as the stage, skipping secondary-market sales, and looks for a dated funding headline that names the account.
Accounts outside your stages take the lower path and are logged in a second tab with the reason.
The second Actor runs one LinkedIn people search per remaining account for your buyer title.
A Code node keeps people whose current employer, or else their headline, names the account and ranks them by your title. Accounts with nobody left are logged with the reason.
A Remove Duplicates node skips anyone a previous run already scored.
The Information Extractor returns a fit score, role, reasons, a why-now line, a subject and an email under 90 words.
Every prospect is appended to Google Sheets, and an IF sends the ones at or above your cut-off to Slack.

Setup
Create a free Apify account, copy the API token from Settings, Integrations, and add it as an Apify credential on the two Actor nodes.
Add an OpenAI credential on the chat model node, or swap in any other chat model.
Connect Google Sheets and point the two Sheets nodes at two tabs: one for prospects, one for skipped accounts.
Connect Slack and pick a channel.
Edit the ICP node: your target accounts (domains match best), the funding stages that buy, the buyer title, your ideal customer and what you sell.
Activate the workflow, or run it once by hand first.

Requirements
An Apify account; the free tier covers a weekly run on a few dozen accounts
An OpenAI API key, or any chat model credential n8n supports
Google Sheets and Slack credentials
No Crunchbase API key, LinkedIn login or data-vendor contract

Customization
buyingStages is a plain list, so add Series D or Venture Round if bigger companies buy from you
Set onlyWithFundingNews to true to only contact accounts with a funding headline inside newsWindowDays
strongFitScore decides who reaches Slack without touching the prompt
peoplePerAccount caps how many people per account go to the model
Change buyerTitle and the ideal customer text to use it for recruiting, partnerships or investor research
Wire the optional Salesforce, HubSpot or Gmail node to the Strong fit output to push prospects into your CRM or inbox

Additional info
Do I need a Crunchbase API key? No. The account check reads public Crunchbase company pages through an Actor, so there is no Crunchbase plan or API key. You get funding rounds, lead investors, headcount bands, industries, headquarters and recent news for each account, which is enough venture capital data to decide who is worth a message this week.

How does it decide an account is in a buying window? Crunchbase lists rounds newest first but does not give round dates. So the stage is the newest round that is not a secondary-market sale. Timing comes from a dated funding headline in the account's news, and headlines about tender offers or secondary sales are ignored because they bring in no new money. A headline only counts when it names the account, because a company's news feed often carries other startups' raises.

How do I find people at a specific company on LinkedIn? The LinkedIn people search step searches public LinkedIn profiles by job title and company, with an optional location. It is the same as searching LinkedIn by company, without a login. One search per account returns a page of up to ten people.

Why are some people dropped? A company search matches anyone whose profile mentions the name, current or past. A name that is also a common word pulls in strangers. In testing, one such search returned ten people and none of them worked there. The template keeps a person only when LinkedIn shows the account as their current employer, or when their headline names it. A headline like "Head of Sales, Linear Technology" is rejected for an account called Linear. The sheet's Employer check column says which test passed.

Does LinkedIn have an API for this? LinkedIn's own APIs do not offer a people search to most developers. This template reads public search results instead, so it needs no LinkedIn account and nothing runs under your name.

Will it pitch the same person twice? No. A Remove Duplicates node remembers every profile it has scored, so a weekly run only sends new people to the model and to Slack.

What does it cost? About $0.008 per account checked on Crunchbase, plus about $0.006 for each account that passes and gets a people search. Twenty accounts a week costs well under $0.50 in Apify charges, plus a few small model calls.

What else can these Actors do? Crunchbase Company API returns funding, investors, founders, key people, similar companies and news for up to 100 companies per run, from a Crunchbase URL, a name or a domain. That makes it a quick company enrichment step for any list. LinkedIn People Search API finds people by name, title, company, school or location, and can open each profile for work history when you turn on enrichment. If you self-host n8n, n8n-nodes-crunchbase-company-api wraps the Crunchbase lookup as a community node.

About Apify. LinkedIn People Search API runs on Apify, a platform of ready-made scrapers and APIs for sources that have no usable public API. Actors are pay per use with no subscription, and they run in the cloud, so nothing runs on your machine and nothing breaks when the source changes its markup.

New to Apify? You can set up a free account and get the API token this template needs in a couple of minutes.

workflows.name: Send a weekly competitor LinkedIn digest with Apify, OpenAI and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Every Monday this reads your competitors' LinkedIn posts and the posts that mention them, and compares each with last week. AI sums up the themes and spots launches, funding or layoffs. Each competitor gets a Google Sheets row. Spikes and announcements alert Slack, and the rest arrive as one digest.

How it works
A Schedule trigger runs every Monday at eight.
A Set node holds your competitors (name, LinkedIn company page, search name), what you sell and the alert rules.
Google Sheets reads last week's row for each competitor, from the same sheet the workflow writes to.
The first Actor reads the past week of posts on each competitor's company page, including the employee posts the page shows.
The second Actor searches public LinkedIn posts that mention each competitor in the same week.
A Code node tags every post with its competitor and drops search results that never name it. Remove Duplicates skips posts that were already counted in an earlier week.
A Code node adds up posts, mentions and engagement per competitor and builds a numbered post list. If nothing could be collected at all, a Slack warning goes out instead.
The Information Extractor writes themes, a two-sentence summary, what changed since last week and one takeaway. It points at any announcement by its post number.
A Code node checks the number against the list and decides between an alert and the digest. Every competitor is appended to Google Sheets.
Alerts go to Slack one by one, with the reason and the post link. The other competitors arrive in one digest message.

Setup
Create a free Apify account, copy the API token from Settings, Integrations, and add it as an Apify credential on both Actor nodes.
Add an OpenAI credential on the chat model node, or swap in any other chat model.
Connect Google Sheets and pick the same spreadsheet and tab on both Sheets nodes.
Connect Slack and pick a channel on all three Slack nodes.
In the Set node, list each competitor's name, LinkedIn company page URL and the name people use for it in posts, and describe what you sell.
Activate the workflow.

Requirements
An Apify account; the free tier covers a weekly run for a handful of competitors
An OpenAI API key, or any chat model credential n8n supports
Google Sheets and Slack credentials
No LinkedIn account, cookie or social listening subscription

Customization
competitors takes a name, a company page URL and a search name each; up to 25 pages and 20 search names per run
search is the phrase looked up in other people's posts. Use the name people actually write, such as "folk CRM" instead of "folk"
spikeFactor, minEngagement and minMentions set what counts as a spike against last week's row
days sets the window; use 1 with a daily schedule for a daily brief
Add your own company to the list to see your posts next to theirs
Add the optional leader posts step, or email the digest instead of posting it

Additional info
How do I monitor competitors on LinkedIn without checking every page? List each competitor's company page once. Every Monday the template reads the past week of posts on each page with a LinkedIn posts API and searches for posts by other people that name them. You get one Slack digest instead of five open tabs, and a separate alert when something actually changed.

What counts as a spike or an announcement? Engagement is likes plus comments on the posts on their page. A competitor alerts when that reaches twice last week's figure and at least 150, when mentions double and reach at least four, or when the model finds a post that announces something new, such as a launch, pricing change, funding, acquisition, partnership, senior hire or layoffs. The model points at the post by its number on a list, and a Code node drops any number that isn't on the list, so an alert always links to a real post.

Is this LinkedIn social listening without a login? Yes. Both Actors read public LinkedIn pages, so you never connect an account or paste a cookie. The mentions step works as a small social listening API for LinkedIn: one row per post with its text, author, date, reactions and comments.

Why are some search results dropped? LinkedIn's post search returns loosely related posts as well as exact matches. The template keeps a result only if the post actually names the competitor. On our test run that dropped one of five results, a post that matched the phrase "folk CRM" without ever saying "folk".

What if LinkedIn hides a competitor's page? Some company feeds aren't shown to signed-out visitors. That competitor is still tracked through the posts that mention it, and the sheet and digest say the page could not be read. If nothing at all can be collected, for example because every URL is wrong, Slack gets a warning instead of an empty digest.

Where does last week's baseline come from? From the same Google Sheet. Each run appends one row per competitor, and the next run reads the latest earlier row back. The first week has nothing to compare with, so only announcements alert that week.

What does it cost? Three competitors cost about 3 cents a week in Apify charges on the free plan and under a cent on a paid plan, plus one small model call per competitor. Search pages seen again within a few days come from a cache and are not charged, and a failed search is never charged.

What else can these Actors do? LinkedIn Posts API returns the recent posts of any public person or company page, or specific posts by URL, with post engagement numbers, tagged companies and top comments. LinkedIn Post Search API finds public posts and articles by keyword, name or hashtag for any date range. If you self-host n8n, n8n-nodes-linkedin-posts-api wraps the posts Actor as a community node.

About Apify. LinkedIn Posts API runs on Apify, a platform of ready-made scrapers and APIs for sources that have no usable public API. Actors are pay per use with no subscription. They run in the cloud, so nothing runs on your machine, and nothing breaks when the source changes its markup.

New to Apify? You can set up a free account and get the API token this template needs in a couple of minutes.

workflows.name: Monitor EU EUDAMED recalls and MDR certificates with Apify, OpenAI and Slack

user.name: Francesco Pacifico
user.bio: Software engineer building HTTP-first Apify Actors & ready-to-run n8n automation pipelines for SecOps/TPRM vendor risk, KYB compliance, public procurement, EU healthcare, and judicial auctions.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to monitor tracked EU EUDAMED UDI-DIs and manufacturer SRNs via Apify, keeps a stateful audit log in an n8n Data Table and Google Sheets, uses OpenAI to triage urgent compliance changes into CAPA guidance, and posts a consolidated alert brief to Slack.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule (or manually in sample mode) and ensures the n8n Data Table used to store EUDAMED regulatory state exists.
Pulls device and expiring MDR certificate data from the Apify “EU EUDAMED Intelligence” actor based on your UDI-DI and SRN watchlists (or generates built-in sample records for testing).
Compares the latest Apify results with the stored state to detect new entities, recalls/FSCAs, conformity or risk changes, and certificate expiry countdown updates, then upserts the current state to the n8n Data Table.
Appends the detected changes to a Google Sheets tab as an audit ledger.
Selects only items that are new, changed, or due for an expiry reminder and sends up to five of the highest-priority items to OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) to generate structured MDR/IVDR urgency, article references, impact summaries, and recommended QA actions.
Emails urgent items to a QA/RA address via Gmail and posts a grouped, consolidated regulatory brief to a Slack channel.
After Slack accepts the message, stamps the corresponding entities in the Data Table as notified/reminded, and if Apify or Slack fails it triggers an error workflow to post a failure alert to Slack.

Setup
Create an Apify token in Apify and add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential that sets Authorization: Bearer , then select it in both Apify HTTP Request steps.
Add credentials for OpenAI, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Slack, and set the Slack channel where the brief and failure alerts should be posted.
Set your Google Sheets document ID and ensure a sheet/tab named EUDAMED_Audit exists for appending the audit log.
Update the watchlist and policy values (UDI-DIs, SRNs, expiry window, reminder days, QA email, and max items) in the configuration step, and optionally test using sampleDay 1 then sampleDay 2 before enabling live Apify calls.
In n8n workflow settings, set this workflow (or a dedicated one) as the error workflow so failures generate the Slack failure alert.

Requirements
n8n 2.48+ with Data Tables enabled (Cloud or self-hosted, core nodes only)
Apify account + API token (francescopacifico1905/eudamed-intelligence Pay-Per-Event)
OpenAI API key, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Slack workspace access

Customization
Adjust remindDaysBefore (90,30,7) or expiringWithinDays in Set UDI-DI Watchlist, SRNs & Alert Policy.
Customize CAPA scoring criteria in AI MDR/IVDR CAPA Triage or raise maxTotalChargeUsd on the Apify nodes for large hospital SKU catalogs.

Additional info
Uses synchronous Pay-Per-Event Apify calls capped at $0.25 per HTTP step; retry-on-fail is intentionally disabled to prevent double billing. Diagnostic NOT_FOUND / INVALID_IDENTIFIER items are never billed by the Actor.

Defines the keywords to compare (for example, your brand and competitors) and the target country/geo.
Calls the Apify Google Trends Scraper API to fetch the last 3 months of interest-over-time and related queries for all keywords on the same 0–100 scale.

workflows.name: Classify company descriptions in batches with Apify Lanseq
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Classify existing company descriptions with your own labels. This workflow batches records through the Lanseq Apify Actor, preserves original IDs, and stops when results are incomplete, so missing records remain visible for review.

How it works
Starts manually and loads the configured labels, budget caps, and input records.
Validates record IDs and text size limits, enforces the execution opt-in and budget constraints, and splits the records into batches of up to 20 items.
Submits the current batch to the Lanseq Actor on Apify as a single run with a per-run maximum charge cap.
Polls the Apify run status every 10 seconds until it reaches a terminal state or a five-minute polling deadline is hit.
When the run finishes, reads the Apify dataset items for that run and joins results back to the original input IDs, flagging missing, duplicate, or unexpected outputs.
Continues with the next batch only if the previous batch succeeded and every row is structure-validated, then outputs a final report that includes all earlier results plus markers for any unsubmitted records.

Setup
Select an existing Apify HTTP Header Auth credential in n8n on Start Actor once, Read run, and Read results. Configure authentication privately in n8n credentials; never put tokens in the workflow JSON or URL.
In Input and budget, replace synthetic records with your own {id, text} items and set classification labels (maximum 20). Keep fields as an empty array for classification. IDs must be unique and at most 100 UTF-8 bytes; each description must be at most 8,000 UTF-8 bytes.
Review the Actor pricing and build 0.1.3, plus the $0.05 per-run and $0.10 total cap defaults. The template is free; Actor execution may incur charges. Set executeModelCalls to true deliberately after reviewing the settings.
Run manually and inspect Final report. Review missing, failed, duplicate or unexpected output and any unsubmitted records. On transport failure, inspect the saved n8n execution and Apify Runs before replaying: a second POST can create another charged run.

Requirements
An n8n instance, an Apify account with access to the Lanseq Actor, an existing Apify authentication credential, and supplied company descriptions. No separate model-provider API key is needed. Source text is sent to Apify and the model service; INPUT and execution logs may retain it.

Customization
Use your own business labels and map a stable ID plus a description from a CRM export or an upstream data workflow. This template does not crawl websites, discover contacts or enrich missing descriptions.

Additional info
Validation: imported and executed in n8n 2.47.7 against an isolated localhost mock API. Checked complete 41-record processing and stopping after partial results; 12 adapter checks passed. The live Apify/model end-to-end path remains unverified. Structurally validated output is not a guarantee of classification accuracy. No pinned execution data or credentials are included. HTTP retries and Actor restart-on-error are disabled; a polling timeout does not cancel the remote run.

Setup and recovery guide: https://github.com/CHYYX/Bridge-ai/blob/lanseq-apify-n8n-20261115/examples/apify-company-classification/README.md

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every 6 hours (or manually) to audit websites listed in Google Sheets using Apify Actors, scores technical SEO, AI search readiness (/llms.txt), DMARC/security, and Google Trends coverage, then uses OpenAI to generate remediation briefs and creates Gmail draft emails while syncing results back to Google Sheets.

How it works
7-Day TTL Queue & Concurrency Lock: Runs every 6 hours (or manually), reads your Google Sheet, prioritizes unaudited websites ahead of bounded retries (Retry_Count  or  heading before launching trend analysis.
Actors #2 & #3 — Parallel CMS/DMARC Stack & Google Trends Breakout Demand: For reachable websites, fans out into two parallel branches joined by a Merge node: (a) Company Domain, Tech Stack & MX/DNS Enricher (xenikii/company-domain-tech-stack-enricher) to detect CMS/framework (Next.js/Vercel, WordPress, Webflow, Shopify, Cloudflare), SPF/DMARC policy, and technical role contacts (webmaster@, dev@, tech@, seo@, hello@), and (b) Google Trends API, Breakout Keywords & Comparison Scraper (xenikii/google-trends-scraper) in explore mode to fetch rising/breakout search queries (+5000%), momentum %, and Knowledge Graph topics.

Guarded Gmail Draft & 29-Column Google Sheets Sync: Creates a Gmail Draft (Alert_Status = Drafted) addressed to the best available contact email once senderName is configured, and writes all 29 audit, scoring, tech stack, trend gap, and report columns back to Google Sheets (or logs bounded retry / Unreachable states).

workflows.name: Extract invoice line items with Funwords document API and VIES VAT check
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow lets users upload an invoice PDF, scan, or photo via an n8n form, extracts header fields and line items using tools.funwords.eu, optionally validates the supplier’s EU VAT number via VIES, and outputs one record per line item plus a downloadable CSV file.

How it works
Receives an uploaded invoice file through an n8n Form trigger.
Sends the file to tools.funwords.eu /document/extract with a configurable list of fields to extract, including line items.
If a supplier VAT number is present, calls tools.funwords.eu /vat/validate (VIES) to validate it and retrieve the registered name when available.
Normalizes the extracted invoice data (and VAT validation result when available) into a single structured invoice object.
Expands the invoice into one output item per line item, repeating invoice-level fields on each row and listing any missing fields.
Converts the line-item rows into a CSV file named invoice-lines.csv for downstream storage or export.

Setup
Create an API key at https://tools.funwords.eu/credits and add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential with Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY.

Update the fields list in the Settings step to match the invoice fields and line-item attributes you want to extract.

workflows.name: Guard workflows and log incidents with the n8n API, data tables and email
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow provides an n8n “safety net” by logging failed workflow executions to an n8n Data Table and sending email alerts, and by fingerprinting workflows nightly or via a secured webhook using the n8n API to detect suspicious edits and store clean versions.

How it works
Triggers when another workflow errors (as an n8n error workflow), on a nightly schedule, or via a Header Auth–protected webhook for before/after edit checks.
Routes the incoming event to either the incident-handling path or the workflow snapshot/guard path based on the payload.
For incidents, extracts key failure details (workflow, execution ID, failed node, error message, and execution URL) and inserts them into an n8n Data Table as a dead-letter log.
Sends an SMTP email alert with the incident details even if the Data Table insert fails.
For snapshots, uses the n8n API to fetch workflows and computes a content-based fingerprint (hash, node count, non-ASCII counts, U+FFFD replacement characters, and question marks).
Compares the current fingerprints to the latest stored fingerprints in an n8n Data Table, stores a new workflow version and updates the latest fingerprint when changes are safe, and flags warnings/errors for suspicious changes.
Emails a report when warnings or errors are detected, and for webhook-driven checks responds with JSON and an HTTP 409 status on errors so calling scripts can stop a deployment.

Setup
Create three n8n Data Tables named workflow_incidents, workflow_versions, and workflow_fingerprints with the columns expected by the insert/upsert steps.
Add credentials for n8n API (to read workflows), SMTP (to send alerts), and Header Auth (to protect the webhook endpoint).
Update the recipient and sender addresses in the workflow settings values (alertTo and alertFrom).
Activate (publish) this workflow so the nightly schedule and the webhook run, then set it as the "Error workflow" in the settings of each workflow you want to protect.
For API-based edits, call the webhook with {"action":"before"|"after","workflowId":""} and ensure your script stops if the response status is 409.

Requirements
n8n with data tables. Tested on n8n 2.47.7 (self-hosted).

user.name: Sedge Labs
user.bio: Sedge Labs is an AI engineering studio in Dubai. We design and build AI agents and automations, in n8n or custom code, where a person approves the steps that matter. For a workflow built around your process, write to hello@sedgelabs.dev.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Checks your competitor YouTube channels every week with Apify and remembers view counts in a Data Table. Flags new outlier videos and older videos that are speeding up, reads the comments on them, has Claude explain why they worked, and sends a digest to Telegram.

How it works
A weekly schedule (Monday 08:00, your n8n instance's timezone) or a manual run starts the Settings node, which holds every value you can change.
A Data Table node creates the memory table on the first run and reads every saved video.
One request to the Apify actor sedgelabs/youtube-channel-scraper gets the latest videos of all channels with exact view counts and publish dates. If this call fails, a short failure notice goes to the delivery step and nothing is saved.
A Code node takes each channel's median views and flags two kinds of video. A new outlier was published within recentDays and has at least outlierMultiple times the median views. A climbing video is older than that window, and its views gained per day since the saved snapshot are at least outlierMultiple times the median daily gain of the channel's other older videos (it needs 3 of them, and it is not flagged again for 4 weeks). The gain must also be at least minClimbPercent percent of the channel's median views per day (0.5 by default), so an old video that gains a few dozen views is not flagged. A video seen for the first time has no gain. A snapshot younger than minHoursBetweenSnapshots is kept as the baseline, so a quick rerun does not erase it.
If anything is flagged, a second Apify request (sedgelabs/youtube-comments-scraper) gets the top comments on those videos, and a Code node picks up to 8 per video: the most liked and the ones that read as questions or requests.
If useClaude is true, Claude writes why each video likely worked (from its title and numbers) and what viewers ask for next (from the picked comments), then one video idea to test. If Claude is off or fails, the digest lists the picked comments instead.
A Code node builds a plain-text digest under 3,500 characters. A week with nothing flagged still gets a short digest with the top gainers.
With deliverTo set to telegram, the digest is sent first. Then every fetched video is saved to the Data Table, and the videos that were in the digest get a reported date. If delivery fails, nothing is saved. With none, the digest is the workflow output.

Setup
Create an Apify account, copy your API token, and add an n8n Header Auth credential with Name Authorization and Value Bearer . Select it on both Apify HTTP Request nodes.
Add an Anthropic credential with your Claude API key and select it on the Ask Claude node.
Open the Settings node and list your competitors in channels (handles, URLs or channel IDs, separated by commas). Change outlierMultiple, recentDays, maxVideosPerChannel, maxVideosInDigest or claudeModel if you want.
To get the digest in Telegram, create a bot with BotFather, add a Telegram credential, select it on the Send digest on Telegram node, and set deliverTo to telegram and telegramChatId in Settings. n8n will not publish a workflow whose Telegram node has no credential, so if you only use none, delete that node and the Send to Telegram? node and connect Build digest to Prepare rows to save.
Execute the workflow once. The first run saves a baseline and reports new outliers only. Daily gains show from the next run that is at least minHoursBetweenSnapshots later. Publish the workflow to run it every Monday.

Requirements
n8n 2.3.0 or later. The Data Table node's table Create operation, which the first run uses, arrived in 2.3.0. Built and tested on n8n 2.45.1.
An Apify account with an API token, and an Anthropic API key (skip it by setting useClaude to false).
A Telegram bot token and chat ID only if deliverTo is telegram.
Apify prices: $0.001 per video row plus $0.001 per exact-details row, so 3 channels at 20 videos each is at most $0.12 a run. The comments actor charges $1.00 per 1,000 comments plus $0.002 per video, so 5 flagged videos at 80 comments each is at most $0.41. A test run on three channels came to about $0.48 at these prices. Claude's cost for the one note is not included.

Customization
Replace the Telegram node with a Slack or Send Email node and use {{ $json.digest }} as the message. Keep it between Send to Telegram? and Prepare rows to save so rows are still saved only after delivery.
Change the Weekly schedule node to another day. Set recentDays to match the gap between runs.
Lower outlierMultiple to flag more videos, or raise it to flag fewer.
Use another tableName per client, or per niche, to keep separate memories.
Give each memory table a name that is not the start of another table's name in the same project. In n8n 2.45.1 the Create table step can fail with "already exists" while a second table with the same name plus "2" exists.
Raise minClimbPercent if older videos are flagged on gains too small to matter, or set it to 0 to turn the floor off.
Rows without an exact view count are left out of the medians and are not saved.

Additional info
By Sedge Labs (sedgelabs.dev). Actors: YouTube Channel Scraper (https://apify.com/sedgelabs/youtube-channel-scraper) and YouTube Comments Scraper (https://apify.com/sedgelabs/youtube-comments-scraper).

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to fetch new and changed EU tender notices from the Apify EU Tenders Scraper (TED), maintains one tracked row per procedure in an n8n Data Table, and posts a single Slack morning brief highlighting changed deadlines/cancellations, due-soon reminders, and new tenders.

How it works
Runs every day at 07:00 (or manually in a sample mode) and loads the configured filters and brief settings.
Pulls only new TED notices from the Apify EU Tenders Scraper (TED) Actor (or generates sample notices for a test run).
Merges the returned notices into an n8n Data Table keyed by procedure, updating existing rows for change notices and creating rows for newly discovered procedures.
Reads all tracked procedures and compiles a Slack-ready brief with three sections: Changed (including old vs. new deadlines and cancellations), Due soon (based on reminder day thresholds), and New.
Posts the brief to a Slack channel, splitting into multiple messages if needed to stay within Slack message length limits.
After Slack accepts each message, updates the corresponding Data Table rows to stamp which tenders were notified/changed/reminded so they are not reposted.
If the Apify search fails, hits the maxItems cap, or Slack rejects a message, stops the run so an Error Trigger posts a failure alert to Slack.

Setup
Install the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify and add an Apify API token credential.
Add a Slack OAuth2 credential with chat:write, set the target channel in both Slack steps (brief and failure alert), and invite the Slack app to that channel.
Review and update the values in “Your settings” (countries, CPV codes, keywords, publishedWithinDays, maxItems, timezone, remindDaysBefore, and changeAlerts).
Ensure the workflow can create and access the n8n Data Table named eu_tender_procedures (it is created automatically on first run).
In n8n Workflow Settings, set the correct timezone and select this workflow as its own Error Workflow so the failure alert runs on errors.
(Optional) Run “Try it with sample notices” and change sampleDay to 2 to test change/deadline behavior without incurring Apify usage.

Requirements
n8n with Data Tables, and the Apify community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify. Tested with: n8n 2.48.2 (Cloud), @apify/n8n-nodes-apify 0.9.0
An Apify account
A Slack workspace where your app may post

Customization
Change the trigger time, the reminder days (remindDaysBefore) or the time zone of the dates (timezone).
Set changeAlerts to deadline to post only moved deadlines and cancellations.
To follow a second market in another copy of the workflow, give that copy's Data Table a different name in its five table nodes.

Additional info
Why it tracks procedures: TED publishes every change to a tender as a new notice with its own number. Of the 42,628 competition notices TED published from 13 October to 12 November 2026, 12,732 (30%) were changes to an earlier notice, and 8,538 of those moved the deadline by a day or more, nearly all of them later, by a median of 7 days. The share of changes differs by country, from 13% to 50% among the ten largest. A monitor keyed on the notice number posts such a tender again as new and keeps counting down to the deadline it saw first.

Limitations: a pause longer than publishedWithinDays misses notices; changing a filter starts a new "Only new notices" history; a tender with lots is one row, and the Actor reports the earliest lot deadline; award notices are not tracked. The table is read in full on every run, so the workflow suits a filtered market (a country, a CPV division), not all of TED. The Code nodes were tested with a day-by-day replay of 12,155 real notices.

Actor used: EU Tenders Scraper on Apify Store — https://kizukidata.com/go/eu-tenders/n8n
Questions or a custom feed: https://kizukidata.com/custom/

workflows.name: Check Gmail e-invoices with Dynamic Document API, Sheets, Drive and DATEV
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors supplier invoice emails in Gmail, validates PDF/XML e-invoices with Dynamic Document API, stores files in Google Drive, maintains an invoice register and supplier list in Google Sheets, sends payment-due reminders by email, and exports ready invoices monthly as a DATEV Buchungsstapel CSV for your accountant.

How it works
Triggers when a new Gmail message matching has:attachment label:incoming-invoices arrives and downloads its attachments.
Splits each email into one item per PDF or XML attachment and validates each file with Dynamic Document API (E-Invoice → Validate) to detect e-invoices and extract invoice data.
Compares validated invoices against the Google Sheets invoice register and supplier list to skip duplicates and assign statuses like ready, new_supplier, on_hold, invalid, no_einvoice, unchecked, or check_failed.
Creates (or reuses) a monthly folder in Google Drive, uploads each invoice file, and appends a row to the Google Sheets invoice register with links to the Drive file and the Gmail message.
Adds newly discovered suppliers to the Google Sheets supplier list, creates Gmail draft replies for invalid/missing e-invoices, and emails alert_email when new invoices need manual review.
Every Monday at 07:00, reads the register and emails alert_email a list of unpaid invoices due within the configured horizon (including overdue items), highlighting invoices that are still on hold.
On the 1st at 06:00, builds a DATEV Buchungsstapel CSV from ready invoices up to the end of the previous month, emails the file to accountant_email, and updates the register rows as exported or book_by_hand.

Setup
Install the verified community node Dynamic Document API from the nodes panel (package @dynamic-document-api/n8n-nodes-dynamic-document-api, 0.1.2 or later, tested with 0.1.2 on n8n 2.44.4, install guide: https://dynamicdocumentapi.com/docs/n8n). Create an API key in the Dynamic Document API dashboard and add it as a Dynamic Document API credential.
Add credentials for Gmail, Google Sheets, and Google Drive (OAuth) and ensure the Gmail trigger query matches your labeling/filtering (default: label:incoming-invoices).
Create a Google Sheet with two tabs, Invoices and Suppliers, using the column headers expected by the workflow, then paste the tab URLs into invoices_sheet_url and suppliers_sheet_url in Inbox settings.
Create a Google Drive parent folder for invoice storage and set its drive_folder_id, plus update company_name, own_vat_id, alert_email, accountant_email, timezone, and (if needed) DATEV parameters like consultant/client numbers and default accounts.
Email yourself a supplier invoice with the label, check the register and the drafts, then publish the workflow.

Requirements
n8n (Cloud or self-hosted) with the verified Dynamic Document API community node 0.1.2 or later (E-Invoice → Validate; if that operation is missing, update the node), tested on n8n 2.44.4
Dynamic Document API account: checking e-invoices is part of every plan, one render per check with a live key; a test key checks 25 a day for free
Google account with Gmail, Google Sheets and Google Drive credentials in n8n
An accountant who works with DATEV, for the monthly export (the register and due list work without it)

Customization
Change the DATEV accounts and tax keys in Inbox settings (datev_default_creditor, datev_default_expense_account, datev_tax_keys); the defaults are SKR03, the note lists SKR04. Per supplier, the supplier list holds the creditor, expense account and a tax key for EU acquisitions and reverse charge
Turn off the request for an e-invoice with ask_for_einvoice, and change due_within_days for the due list
Edit the wording of the draft replies in Check supplier, IBAN and duplicates
Swap Gmail for Outlook or IMAP, or Google Sheets for another table

Additional info
Tested against the live API with real e-invoices: XRechnung CII, a ZUGFeRD PDF with two VAT rates, a UBL credit note, goods from an Austrian supplier (intra-EU acquisition), services from a Dutch supplier with a new IBAN (reverse charge), an XML with a wrong total, a plain PDF and the same invoice sent twice. Each ended in the expected status, draft or skip; a second run of the same emails added nothing. The DATEV file passed the field patterns of DATEV's format check program, and a second export found nothing to book. Replies are always drafts. The JSON contains no credentials or private IDs. Agree the DATEV accounts and tax keys with your accountant before the first import.

Quick overview
This workflow runs every weekday morning, searches for newly posted jobs across Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, and Workday career sites via Apify, then posts a digest to Slack and appends each job to Google Sheets.

How it works
Runs every weekday at 8:00 AM based on a cron schedule.
Sets the search criteria such as keywords, locations, remote preference, posting window, and maximum job count.
Calls the Apify ATS jobs search actor to fetch only new job postings that match the criteria.
Filters the results to keep only valid job records with a title.
Formats up to 40 jobs into a single Slack message and posts the digest to a selected Slack channel.
Maps job fields (title, company, location, remote, postedAt, ATS, applyUrl) and appends them as new rows in Google Sheets.

Setup
Create an Apify account, generate an API token, and add it in n8n as an HTTP Header Auth credential (Authorization: Bearer ) for the Apify request.
Update the search inputs (keywords, locations, remote, postedWithinDays, maxJobs, and stateStoreName) to match what you want to track.
Connect your Slack credential and choose the channel to post the digest to.
Create a Google Sheet with columns: title, company, location, remote, postedAt, ats, applyUrl, then paste the sheet URL into the Google Sheets node and confirm the target sheet tab name.
